utterance: Hi Mark, I'm Dr Chen. I hear you've been feeling pretty rotten with a cough and fever. Can you tell me more — when did this start, and how has it changed day to day?
reply: It started three days ago with a dry, hacking cough, and I have been burning up on and off. Since yesterday I have started bringing up stuff that is a rusty, brownish colour, though it was clear at first. I also got a sharp pain low down on the right side round towards my back yesterday, which catches me when I take a deep breath or cough. It feels worse than the first day, but about the same since yesterday, so I am not going downhill fast.

utterance:
Mark, the news is clear: you have pneumonia — an infection in the lower part of your right lung. The chest X-ray shows a patch of inflamed lung, which matches your rusty phlegm, fever and the pain when you breathe deeply. The good news is your oxygen level and blood pressure are reasonable, so you can be treated at home rather than in hospital. I've prescribed two antibiotics — amoxicillin capsules (one, three times a day) and doxycycline tablets (one, twice a day) — both for 5 days, to cover the usual pneumonia bugs. Take the doxycycline with food, avoid heavy sun exposure while on it, and finish the whole course even when you start feeling better (which should be within 48–72 hours). Rest, fluids, and paracetamol for the fever and pain are fine. It's a good idea to get the flu shot and a COVID booster once you're recovered.

Please come back or go to hospital straight away if: your breathing gets more difficult, your oxygen sense drops (feeling faint or blue lips), fever or the rusty phlegm doesn't improve after 2–3 days of antibiotics, you cough up blood, get chest pain not linked to breathing/coughing, become confused, or feel much worse in any way. Also, if the cough lingers more than a few weeks after treatment, we'll re-check you. Any questions before I write this up?
reply: Pneumonia? Blimey, I didn't think it was that serious. I just need to get these tablets and get back to school before things get completely out of hand with the maths exams.

utterance: I know it sounds scary, but caught early like this it responds well to antibiotics. That said — please don't push through it. Take today and tomorrow off at minimum, rest and drink plenty of fluids, and you should be feeling markedly better within a couple of days. If you don't improve by day 3, or if anything I mentioned earlier happens (worsening breathlessness, confusion, coughing blood), come straight back. Take care, Mark, and I hope the maths exams go smoothly too!
reply: Right, I will take it easy. Thanks, doc.
